column-parallel.d: A tensor-parallel linear layer in which the columns of \(W\) (the outputs) are divided among the ranks: each rank computes its slice of \(Y = XW\) without any communication. QKV (by heads) and gate/up are column-parallel.

par-megatron.d: The Megatron-LM pattern: a column-parallel layer, an elementwise function, then a row-parallel layer. The sliced output of the first feeds the second directly, and the whole pair costs a single all-reduce.

world-size.d: Number of GPU processes in one engine replica. In vLLM, TP × PP (× prefill context parallel). DP multiplies whole replicas, each with its own processes (DP × PP × TP workers in total). EP and DCP reuse ranks that already exist.

coletiva.d: A communication operation in which every rank in a group takes part and nobody finishes before everyone arrives (all-reduce, all-gather, reduce-scatter, all-to-all). That's why the step moves at the pace of the slowest rank.

all-gather.d: A collective in which each rank contributes one piece and everyone receives the concatenation. It joins the logits of a vocab-parallel lm_head and the (score, id) candidates of a distributed top-k.

reduce-scatter.d: A collective that sums the tensors of all ranks and hands each one only a slice of the sum. An all-reduce is equivalent to reduce-scatter + all-gather, and Megatron's sequence parallel takes advantage of the interval between the two.

all-to-all.d: A collective in which each rank sends a different piece to every other rank. It's the transport for dispatching tokens to the experts' owners under EP with DP > 1.

expert-parallel.d: Distributing whole experts across the ranks (Qwen: 256 of 512 per GPU; GLM TP3: 96 of 288) instead of cutting each expert. With DP = 1 the tokens are already replicated and the collective is still TP's all-reduce.

expert-map.d: A table that translates an expert's global id into the local index of the rank that stores it, or marks that it doesn't live there (−1 or a sentinel). It has to be on the device to fit inside CUDA graphs.

dispatch-combine.d: The two moves of an MoE with EP and DP > 1: sending each token to the ranks that own its experts and bringing the outputs back to the originating rank. Done by all-to-all or by all-gather + reduce-scatter (--all2all-backend).

pipeline-parallel.d: Splitting the layers into stages, one per node; only the activation crosses each boundary. It doesn't add up the nodes' bandwidths on the same token, so it doesn't reduce decode latency.

bolha-de-pipeline.d: The idle time of the stages while the microbatches fill and drain the pipeline: a fraction \((p-1)/(m+p-1)\) with \(p\) stages and \(m\) microbatches.

microlote.d: A piece of the batch that goes through the pipeline independently, so that different stages can work at the same time on different microbatches.

data-parallel.d: Whole replicas of the model (in vLLM, one EngineCore per replica), each serving its own requests, with no communication in the forward pass. It requires the model to fit in each replica.

replicado.d: A tensor stored whole on every rank instead of sliced: MLA's KV latent, indexers, routers, hyper-connections. It costs no communication, but each rank reads the whole copy at every step.

kv-replicado.d: A KV cache stored whole on every TP rank. It happens when there's a single KV head (MLA/MQA): the second node doesn't split the KV, it only frees memory by splitting the weights.

vocab-parallel-embedding.d: Embedding and lm_head sliced into contiguous id ranges: each rank looks up, or projects, only its own range. The embedding is joined by an all-reduce; the logits, by an all-gather or by an argmax over (value, id) pairs.

divisibilidade-tp.d: The requirement that every sliced axis (heads, intermediate, vocabulary, and the quantization blocks of the local shape) be a multiple of the TP degree. When it fails: padding, EP, or replication.

draft-tp.d: The drafter's tensor-parallel degree in speculative decoding (draft_tensor_parallel_size): equal to the target's (splits the reads, pays collectives) or 1 (one rank does everything, the others wait).

imposto-de-divisibilidade.d: The GLM README's expression (“the divisibility tax”) for the cost of running the DFlash2 drafter at TP = 1 on TP3, because its 32 query heads and 8 KV heads don't divide by 3.

latency-bound.d: The regime in which a collective's time is dominated by the fixed latency \(\alpha\), not by the bytes: messages much smaller than \(\alpha\beta\). That's the case for decode all-reduces (5–64 KB).

modelo-alfa-beta.d: The communication cost model \(T(n) = \alpha + n/\beta\): a fixed latency per message plus bytes over bandwidth. The knee at \(n^\star = \alpha\beta\) separates the latency regime from the bandwidth regime.

top-k-distribuido.d: A top-k computed in parts: each rank picks the top-k of its slice, the (score, id) pairs are gathered by an all-gather, and the top-k of the union equals the global top-k. Used by DeepSeek's SP indexer and by DCP.

kv-por-dono.d: Splitting the KV cache by conversation rather than by token: each conversation lives on one rank (its owner), which keeps its latents and computes its attention in decode. It saves MLA's replicated copy with no per-layer merge, at the price of balancing conversations by placement (e.g., the GLM·TF recipe's patch 0129, 6,204 → 3,300 B per token per Spark).
